blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Dress codes in the UK are not the same everywhere. They depend on the industry and the office. Traditional sectors — banking, law and insurance — still like a suit and tie. Creative or tech offices are more relaxed. They are often smart casual or just casual.

Here is a safe rule for a new joiner: dress a little more formally on day one. Then watch what the senior people wear, and adjust. Clean, neat and well fitted matter more than expensive.

The British rarely comment on your clothes. But they quietly notice.

items.q: According to the text, which sectors still like a suit and tie?
items.why: "Traditional sectors — banking, law and insurance — still like a suit and tie."

items.q: What should a new joiner do on day one?
items.why: "dress a little more formally on day one."

items.q: According to the text, what matters more than expensive clothes?
options: Clean, neat and well fitted clothes
items.why: "Clean, neat and well fitted matter more than expensive."

items.q: "They quietly notice." This suggests that the British…
options: do not care about clothes at all
wear the same clothes every day
see your clothes even when they say nothing
items.why: Inferência: eles raramente comentam, mas reparam em silêncio — as roupas contam.

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which idea?
options: You should watch the senior people and adjust.
One dress code is correct for every UK office.
Neat clothes are important on day one.
The right clothes depend on the office.
items.why: Inferência: o texto todo diz que o código de vestimenta muda de setor para setor.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Charlotte falando com a nova colega. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Hi! Welcome to the team. Let me help you with your first week. Our office is here in the City of London, and it is a traditional one. We work with banks, so people dress formally.

For your first day, I would wear a suit. You do not need a tie, but a jacket is a good idea. Keep it simple. Clean and neat is more important than expensive. A dark colour is always safe.

After a few days, look around. Watch what the senior people wear, and copy that. If they are a little more relaxed, you can be too. But it is better to start smart and then adjust.

One more thing. In this office, nobody will say anything about your clothes. That is very British! But they do notice. Good clothes give you credibility before you even speak. So on day one, dress with a little more care. You will feel more confident. Any questions? Just ask me any time this week.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What kind of office does Charlotte describe?
options: A traditional office in the City of London
items.why: "Our office is here in the City of London, and it is a traditional one."

items.q: What does Charlotte suggest for the first day?
options: A suit, and a jacket is a good idea
The same clothes as at home
items.why: "For your first day, I would wear a suit… a jacket is a good idea."

items.q: After a few days, what should the new colleague do?
options: Ask the manager for a uniform
Watch the senior people and copy them
items.why: "Watch what the senior people wear, and copy that."

items.q: Charlotte says nobody will talk about your clothes. She means…
options: you can wear anything you like
people still notice, even without talking
the office has no dress code
items.why: Inferência: ninguém comenta, mas todos reparam — por isso ela dá o conselho.

items.q: Why does Charlotte say good clothes give you credibility?
options: Because they help before you even speak
Because the boss chooses your clothes
items.why: "Good clothes give you credibility before you even speak." A boa impressão começa antes da fala.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Every office has its own dress code." A dress code is…
options: the rules about what to wear
items.why: Dress code = código de vestimenta, as regras sobre o que vestir.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "On day one, wear a ___ and a tie for a formal office."
items.why: Suit = terno, a peça formal para escritórios tradicionais.

items.q: "His clothes were always clean and neat." Neat means…
items.why: Neat = arrumado, limpo e bem cuidado.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "She is a ___, so this is her first week in the company."
items.why: New joiner = recém-chegado, quem acabou de entrar na empresa.

items.q: "A tech office is often smart casual." Smart casual means…
items.why: Smart casual = casual elegante: relaxado, mas ainda arrumado.

blocks.instruction: Expressões úteis no trabalho. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Take a jacket, just to be on the safe side." This means…
options: to be careful and avoid a problem
items.why: Be on the safe side = por segurança, para não correr risco.

items.q: "Watch the team and fit in." To fit in means to…
items.why: Fit in = se enturmar, combinar com o grupo.

items.q: "Start smart, then you can dress down later." To dress down means to…
items.why: Dress down = vestir-se de forma mais casual.

items.q: "Don't worry, you will soon settle in." To settle in means to…
options: get used to the new place
items.why: Settle in = se adaptar, se acostumar ao novo lugar.

items.q: "Your first day helps you make a good impression." This means to…
options: make people like and respect you
items.why: Make a good impression = causar boa impressão.
